plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, the optimal action is straightforward: bid exactly my value of $30.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding higher than your value risks overpaying (winning at a loss), while bidding lower only risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $7, the optimal action is to bid exactly $7 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $36 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid (profitable), and lose when it doesn't (avoiding a loss). This maximizes expected profit.
